name: Cygnus
introduction: is the Swan, flying with outstretched wings down the Milky Way. Its brightest stars form the Northern Cross, and its tail star, Deneb, is a corner of the Summer Triangle. It is best seen high overhead on northern summer and autumn evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Cygnus lies along the plane of our galaxy, where dark dust lanes, called the Great Rift, split the glowing band of the Milky Way in two. Looking through the Swan, we are looking along the Orion Arm, the spiral arm in which the Sun sits.

It is also a landmark of modern astronomy. In 1838, Friedrich Bessel measured the parallax of [61 Cygni](id:10pc-0029), the first star whose distance was ever determined. Cygnus X-1, discovered in 1964, became the first object widely accepted as a black hole: about 21 times the mass of the Sun, orbiting a blue supergiant. From 2009 to 2013, NASA’s Kepler space telescope stared at a patch of sky between Cygnus and Lyra and found thousands of planets around other stars.

image.caption: Star View schematic · catalogue positions, north up and east left
image.alt: Vega, Deneb and Altair form the Summer Triangle. Vega and Altair are nearby, while Deneb is about 1,400 light-years away.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Deneb](hip:102098) appears only slightly fainter than Vega and Altair, yet it is about 1,400 light-years away, more than fifty times farther. To shine that brightly from so far away, this white supergiant must be one of the most luminous stars visible to the naked eye, tens of thousands of times brighter than the Sun.

[Albireo](hip:95947), the Swan’s beak, is a favorite of small telescopes: a golden star with a sapphire-blue companion. Whether the two are truly bound together or just line up by chance is still debated.
[Sadr](hip:100453) is at the center of the cross, with [Aljanah](hip:102488) and [Fawaris](hip:97165) along the wings.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Cygnus is crowded with nebulae: the North America Nebula, a glowing cloud near Deneb shaped like the continent; the Veil Nebula, the lacy remains of a supernova that exploded thousands of years ago; and the Crescent Nebula, a bubble blown by a powerful Wolf–Rayet star.
